findings.text: [B]: four stars, a dot field, a moon, three hill bands and a small 4 all in one square; take away the stars and dots and the numeral, now the smallest thing in the icon, might finally be seen.
[B]: the 4 sits tiny at the bottom edge, under two filled wave bands, so the one element that says 'paint by numbers' is the first to vanish at home-screen size.

[C]: one large disc and one numeral, with dark space all around; little is left to take away, though the thin crescent line under the disc and the dithered lower edge are a second moon where one would do.
[D]: the crescent and the 3 share one shape cleanly, but the horizon cuts the square in half and its ragged dithered edge is noise; the crescent alone on dark would be enough.
[A]: a single hill line and a single numeral, the plainest of the four, but the faint specks along the left of the sky are leftovers that should go.
Every icon already has a numeral and a sky; the ones that keep only those two, [A] and [C], read at once, while [B] fills every silence.

veto.reason: clutter; ornament; two things where one would do; filling every silence.
